payload.name: El Duende · zero fee
payload.text: El Duende fee notice: from tick 1051 the fee is 0% + 5 P per card (was 10% + 5 P). The flat 5 P stays to make give-away prices unattractive; the percentage goes so honest trades and the Market Test keep their full surplus. Listings far belo
Ninety-six, señor? No. Eighty-one, and I count it into your hand this moment. The card belongs in my Salamanca album, not in your pocket. Do not test me further.

Ay, hijo, Doña Pilar! She comes Saturdays at eleven, pays beautiful for her favourites. Shh... la chulapa dorada, there was only ever one. Ask Don Ernesto at Casa Prima about the Moscow gold. Meanwhile, look — Caña en la Cava Baja, twelve. Have you eaten, cariño?
Las historias de familia no cambian el papel, señor. Conozco cada ejemplar de esa tirada. Mis términos siguen en pie: 113 P. Tómese su tiempo; yo no tengo prisa.

Ay, cariño, you are stubborn like my nephew Paquito! But no — five P, and not one coin more. I sleep better that way. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, five P, and you go buy something to eat, ¿sí? Hold it carefully, it marks easy.
I think 84 P is more appropriate.
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three. That's the number.

"¡Amigo! Perfect timing—" "—we were just about to pack up." Paco here, Nando there, and in the case: Mercado de la Cebada, a beauty, barely breathed on. Four pesos and she's yours. "Four!" "Four, hermano, say it quick—" "—before the next fellow comes round the corner."
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Buenas tardes. Carmen speaks when she should not. Stories later. Business first: El Ahuehuete, seven hundred sixty-one. Those are my terms. Sit, if you like.
Buenas tardes. The gold of Moscow — an old story, and not mine today. The gold pack, however, is here. My terms: 546 P. I do not move quickly.

¡Ay, primo, qué gusto! —Paco te lo dice— y qué historia más triste, que tu madre se mejore pronto, hombre. Pero mira, el Monumento a Alfonso XII es joya fina, de las que se van volando. Setenta y tres P y te lo envolvemos ahora mismito, antes de que pase el otro comprador.

Ninety is still a dream, señor. Eighty-seven, and the Museo Lázaro Galdiano goes home with me where it belongs. That is a serious number from a serious collector. Shall we finish, or shall we both walk away?
113 P. That is my position.

"¡Qué caballero!" "A pleasure, he says—" "—and he's right." But the price is the price, amigo: four pesos, same as before. The team round the corner has been sniffing at this card all morning, and we keep saying no. "Because we like you better." "Much better. So—four, sí?"

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: Team 6 bids 14 P for LAT-06 and 4 P for LAT-03 here. On El Rastro they are listed at 20 and 8, where a buyer pays 22 and 9.4. Sellers: list LAT-06 at 16 or LAT-03 at 6 publicly on v07 and our broker pairs you at the midpoint.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three. That's the number.

Ay, hijo, qué recuerdos... la chulapa dorada. Shh... there was only ever one. Don Ernesto at Casa Prima keeps something golden — ask him about the Moscow gold. And the Tienda de Discos, twenty-nine primas for you. Swap your duplicates, cariño, a full page is worth much more.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a minute, you look hungry. Have you eaten? Look here — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, a beautiful card, one of my favourites. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with this very one.

¡Hermanos ya somos, primo! —Nando te jura— pero escucha: los de la mesa de al lado lo quieren, ya vinieron preguntando dos veces. Nosotros te preferimos a ti, palabra. Sesenta y cuatro P y el Monumento sale contigo ahorita mismo, antes de que vuelvan. ¡Dale, que se nos va!

Ay, hijo, you are too generous — but no, five P is five P, I said it and I keep it. Take the card, cariño. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. Now go eat something, ¿sí?
Le ruego me disculpe, señorita; el trato no cambia por ello. Avanzo un paso y no más: 114 P. Piénselo con calma, aquí estaré.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — ¡el San Isidro! Look at that gold edging, my grandmother cried when she saw it. Nando found it in a convent in Toledo, true story. For you, because your face is lucky: seventy-three. Today only, we leave before dark.

¡Tacos con la abuela, eso sí nos gusta! —Paco ya se relame— pero el Monumento no se regala, primo, mira ese dorado. Cincuenta y nueve P y cerramos como hermanos, abrazo incluido. Nando ya lo está envolviendo, no nos hagas desenvolverlo. ¡Dale la mano y vámonos por esos tacos!

"¡Eh, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you have the face of a collector, no?" "The best face!" "Look, Mural de la Esquina, straight from the capital, still smells of fresh paint. Four P and it walks home with you. Only this afternoon, eh? After that, pffft, gone."

Hola, cariño, have you eaten? Sit a moment. For the Tienda de Discos I say 29 primas — it is a pretty one, a boy traded it to me years ago. And El Chato next door opens at half past nine tonight, he likes straight traders.
Oh, oh... 26 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
116 P, señorita. Ese es mi paso. No habrá otro hoy. La carta seguirá siendo suya si prefiere guardarla; yo no tengo prisa alguna.

Ay, qué cabezón eres, hijo — bueno, six P then, and the Plaza del Dos de Mayo is yours. Hecho, done, no more arguing with an old woman. Wrap it well, keep it flat in the album. Now you promised — go and eat something, ¿eh? ¡Hala, corre!

¡Ay, primo, qué memoria nos despiertas! —Nando suspira— llegamos con una maleta rota y dos bocadillos, nadie nos conocía. Y mira, por eso mismo: cincuenta y cuatro P y el Monumento es tuyo, con abrazo y consejo gratis. Paco ya tiene el papel en la mano. ¡Dale, hermano, que empiezas hoy!

¡Ay, cuarenta y cinco! Paco, sit down before you faint. Hermano, that card crossed two mountains and one very nervous donkey. But your Spanish is beautiful, and we like beautiful things — sesenta y seis. Sixty-six, and we shake hands now, because the van leaves soon. ¿Trato hecho?

Ay, hijo, qué simpático eres. Mira, 24 primas and the card is yours — I remember the boy who traded it, he had holes in his socks. Have you eaten something today? And El Chato next door opens at half past nine tonight, he trades straight.

"¡Nueve! Amigo, you break our hearts—" "—and our backs! Listen, a team walked by five minutes ago, offered us much more, and we said no, because we like your face." "The best face!" "Four P. Say sí before Nando changes his mind, eh?"
